editionContext.scope: The story of Rostam and Sohrab whole, from Rostam’s hunt to the mourning in Zabul: thirty steps over the twenty-one sections of the Ganjoor text, each step resting on its sections.
editionContext.evidencePolicy: Use actual verse for narrative assertions. Site-generated AI summaries and museum story synopses are not the selected base text.

entities.label: Rostam and Sohrab
entities.summary: The story of Sohrab in Ferdowsi’s Shahnameh. It begins when Rostam goes hunting and loses his horse Rakhsh, and follows him to Samangan.

events.label: The poet reflects before the tale
events.summary: The poet ponders death, fate and justice, and then announces the story he is about to tell.

events.label: Rostam rides out to hunt
events.summary: Rostam, in low spirits, rides to the border of Turan, hunts wild asses, roasts one and falls asleep while Rakhsh grazes.

events.label: Rakhsh is taken
events.summary: A small band of Turkish riders finds the grazing horse, captures it and leads it away; Rostam wakes to find it gone and sets out on foot.

events.label: A welcome in Samangan
events.summary: Following the tracks, Rostam reaches Samangan; its king and nobles greet him, promise to find the horse and host him at a feast.

events.label: A visitor in the night
events.summary: Late at night a young woman enters his chamber, names herself as the king's daughter and tells Rostam why she has come.

events.label: A marriage is arranged
events.summary: Rostam has a priest ask her father for her hand, and the king gladly gives her to him with due ceremony.

events.label: A keepsake and a farewell
events.summary: At dawn Rostam leaves her a famous token from his arm with instructions for a future child, the horse is returned and he departs.

events.label: A son is born and grows
events.summary: Nine months later Tahmineh bears a son, names him Sohrab, and he grows with astonishing speed and strength.

events.label: Sohrab asks about his father
events.summary: At ten Sohrab demands to know his lineage; his mother tells him who his father is, shows tokens sent from Iran and urges secrecy toward Afrasiab.

events.label: A plan to march on Iran
events.summary: Sohrab declares he will raise a Turkish army, unseat Kay Kavus, set his father on the throne and then turn on Afrasiab; warriors gather to him.

events.label: Afrasiab sends his captains
events.summary: Afrasiab welcomes the news, chooses twelve thousand riders under Human and Barman and secretly orders that father and son must not learn of each other.

events.label: Hojir falls at the White Castle
events.summary: Sohrab's army reaches the White Castle; its keeper Hojir rides out alone, is thrown from the saddle, asks for quarter and is sent bound to Human.

events.label: Gordafarid rides out
events.summary: Gazhdaham's daughter Gordafarid arms herself in secret and fights Sohrab; when caught she reveals her face, and by a ruse regains the castle and mocks him from the walls.

events.label: The castle is abandoned
events.summary: Old Gazhdaham writes to the king describing the young champion, then leads the garrison away by night; next morning Sohrab finds the castle empty.

events.label: The king summons Rostam
events.summary: Kay Kavus and his lords resolve to send Giv to Zabul with a letter; Rostam receives it but lingers three days feasting before setting out.

events.label: The king's anger and a reconciliation
events.summary: Angered by the delay, Kay Kavus orders Rostam and Giv hanged; Rostam strikes Tus aside and leaves, and Gudarz persuades both sides to make peace over a feast.

events.label: The Iranian host arrives
events.summary: The king's army marches to the castle and pitches its tents; Human is alarmed, but Sohrab sees no equal among them and calls for wine.

events.label: A night visit in disguise
events.summary: Rostam enters the castle in Turkish dress, watches Sohrab at his banquet and kills Zhende Razm who questions him; on the way back he meets Giv and reports to the king.

events.label: Questions about the banners
events.summary: From a height Sohrab makes the captive Hojir name the owners of each pavilion and banner; Hojir names many but withholds one name.

events.label: A challenge to the king
events.summary: Sohrab rides to the Iranian camp, taunts Kay Kavus, tears up stakes of the royal pavilion; the king sends Tus to call on Rostam, who arms himself.

events.label: Face to face
events.summary: The two champions meet apart from the armies; Sohrab asks the older man whether he is Rostam, and he answers that he is not.

events.label: The first day of combat
events.summary: They fight with spears, swords, maces and bows until both are spent, then each charges the other's army, and they agree to resume at dawn.

events.label: Counsel in the night
events.summary: Sohrab and Human weigh the day; Rostam tells Kay Kavus of the young man's strength, then gives his brother Zavareh instructions for the morrow.

events.label: Suspicion and an offer of peace
events.summary: Sohrab tells Human he suspects his opponent, and at dawn asks the champion to lay down arms and reveal his lineage; Rostam refuses.

events.label: The first wrestling bout
events.summary: They wrestle on foot; Sohrab throws Rostam, who escapes by claiming a custom that spares a man thrown once; Rostam washes, prays and returns.

events.label: The second bout and a token
events.summary: In the second bout Rostam throws Sohrab and stabs him; the dying youth speaks of his father, and the keepsake on his arm reveals who he is.

events.label: Grief in both camps
events.summary: The Iranians first fear Rostam dead; Sohrab asks him to spare the Turanian army, and the lords hold Rostam back when he turns a dagger on himself.

events.label: A plea for the remedy
events.summary: Rostam sends Gudarz to ask Kay Kavus for the healing elixir; the king refuses, fearing the strength of father and son together.

events.label: Lament on the field
events.summary: Word comes that Sohrab is dead; Rostam laments, burns his pavilion and asks that the Turanians be spared, and Kay Kavus agrees.

events.label: The return to Zabul
events.summary: Rostam brings the coffin home to Zabul, where Zal and the nobles mourn; a tomb is built and Bahram speaks words of counsel.

reviewNotes: No historical or BCE dates are assigned to literary events, lifespans, or places.

A source-backed statement is not a declaration of historical fact; all narrative claims belong to the selected literary world.
